transcript: Security Forces Airmen have the tough task of protecting assets on base, including the airmen. But like anything, doing a good job takes practice. Members of the 86th Security Forces Squadron and their brethren from the 569th Security Forces Squadron came together to conduct training on the collapsible ASP baton. Training to me was good. It was useful. If I ever get in a combat situation where I need to pull out my baton, I'm confident that I can pull it out and get the individual on the ground to cooperate. The training showed students how and where to strike with the weapon when it's open or closed. They also learned how to tell when it's necessary to use the weapon on an individual. And now they put their hands up and they want to fight. You know, and now you're there, you're standing in front of this person with their hands up, and they're showing aggression as though they want to fight and they want to cause, you know, maybe some bodily harm to somebody. And that's the time when you will utilize that ASP baton. Proper training goes a long way towards preparing airmen to defend themselves and members of the Kaiserslautern military community. Senior Airman Marvin Wickfall, Ramstein Air Base, Germany.
